source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed the primary Poosala histogram, HyperLogLog, and self-tuning histogram papers; PostgreSQL 18 planner-statistics, pg_stats, ANALYZE, CREATE STATISTICS, and statistics-security documentation; current MySQL 8.4 histogram, SQLite ANALYZE, and SQL Server statistics documentation. Checked histogram layouts, MCV exclusion, targets/sampling, multivariate kinds, HLL error regime, feedback bias, security, and product-specific representation differences.

evidence: Checked N/n, actual/estimate, selectivity, null/MCV/residual mass, NDV, bucket, density, RSE, q-error, and generation definitions.
Checked denominators and null/non-null/residual domains are explicit.
Checked exact counts, sample estimators, compressed models, sketches, feedback, and staleness remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Bucket endpoints, collation, cumulative versus per-bucket mass, and zero policies are required rather than assumed.

evidence: Recomputed 16-row null, MCV, residual, NDV, equality, range, and mass-conservation values.
Recomputed rare-value miss probability near 0.367861 and 50-fold correlation error.
Recomputed Exercise 1 residual mass/selectivity and row estimates.
Reviewed disjoint null/MCV/residual mass partition.
Reviewed histogram coverage/interpolation assumptions and simple-sample miss formula.
Reviewed sketch compatibility, dependency, atomic publication, and feedback-label invariants.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: HLL 1.04/sqrt(m) is attributed to the original estimator regime, not presented as a universal interval.

evidence: Reviewed empty, all-null, constant, unique, duplicate-heavy, rare, heavy-hitter, sparse, NaN, out-of-range, ascending-key, and zero estimate/actual cases.
Reviewed correlated, dependent, mutually exclusive, partition-skewed, expression, filtered, inherited, and global/local populations.
Reviewed biased samples/feedback, timeouts/censoring, incompatible sketches, partial refresh, schema change, catalog/operator leakage, tenant poisoning, and privacy budgets.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown or inconsistent summaries require fallback/default or recollection, not fabricated precision.

evidence: Checked identity/snapshot/method/sample/target/version bind every statistic.
Checked frequencies, bounds, masses, domains, MCV exclusion, and sketch compatibility.
Checked generation validation/atomicity and feedback provenance/tenant controls.
invariant_checking.notes: Statistics never substitute for enforced integrity constraints.

evidence: Reviewed exact finite mass proof and residual equality derivation.
Reviewed why sample size does not cure biased inclusion and independence is a model rather than identity.
Reviewed mergeability and generation publication obligations.
proof_review.notes: Estimator accuracy and plan benefit require empirical evaluation beyond accounting proofs.

evidence: The executable is labeled an exact finite summary, not a sampler or production estimator.
Rare-miss exponential comparison is labeled an approximation.
Product behavior and paper results are attributed without universalizing their formats or guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Model, exact fact, estimate, heuristic, empirical result, and operational policy are separated.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact fourteen-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded Python 3.14.4 toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced finite accounting, rare miss, correlation error, and exercise arithmetic.
All eleven source artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-063 and local links were checked.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No database ANALYZE, population sample, histogram build, HLL trial, multivariate estimator, feedback loop, security operator, plan comparison, production workload, or external review was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed population identity, sampling, mass decomposition, histogram designs, NDV/sketches, dependencies, physical correlation, maintenance, partition/global merging, feedback, evaluation, security, and diagnosis.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed collection/refresh budgets, sample and generation metadata, conservative compatibility, atomic publication, held-out workload evaluation, first-divergence diagnosis, tenant/privacy controls, canaries, fallback, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives statistics from a population contract, executes exact mass accounting, compares histogram/NDV/dependency approaches, covers fourteen misconceptions and ten distinct examples, and advances five exercises to a distributed multitenant statistics service with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external query-optimizer researcher, statistician, database maintainer, sketch/histogram specialist, privacy/security reviewer, distributed-systems operator, or educator review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither production sampling accuracy, histogram/sketch correctness, arbitrary mergeability, universal selectivity accuracy, plan optimality, workload representativeness, privacy, certification, nor deployment fitness.
